subject: Packaging credit rebalancing — playbook errata
messages:
From: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@acrohealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: AcroHealth Procurement <procurement@acrohealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:23:00-08:00
Subject: Packaging credit rebalancing — errata on order form

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. We ran it by our finance team and they've pushed back on the packaging credit schedule in Exhibit B. In short: they want a smoother release of credits (to avoid a large upfront credit that would distort Q1 forecasts) and a clearer clawback definition tied to net usage vs committed tiers.

I've attached our redline (AcroHealth_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf) with inline comments — key asks are:
- Convert 100% upfront packaging credit to a 70%/30% release over two quarters tied to usage thresholds.
- Remove the unilateral clawback language (Section 4.3) and replace with a mutual true-up based on documented usage within 45 days after quarter end.
- Add an escrow holdback option (up to 10% of credits) for the first 2 quarters for new integrations.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on each of these? We're trying to finalize before our year-end procurement window (target 2026-11-25).

Thanks,
Susan Lewis
Director, Procurement
AcroHealth

Attachments: AcroHealth_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@acrohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging credit rebalancing — errata on order form

Susan —

Appreciate the redline and the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Ben (finance) to weigh in on the contractual language and P&L impact. Quick initial responses below, we'll follow up formally after internal review:

- 70%/30% release: operationally reasonable; need to confirm how you want thresholds defined (absolute tokens / embeddings / API calls).
- Clawback → mutual true-up: happy to move to mutual true-up language but need clarity on evidence and timing (we typically ask for 60 days to reconcile with our usage logs).
- Escrow holdback (10%): finance flagged this as material; if applied, we need a defined release schedule and a clear remediation path for integration failures.

Can we schedule a 30-minute quick call Wednesday to run through triggers? If we agree on the mechanics, Marissa will draft a limited-scope amendment rather than a full rework of Exhibit B.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Quoted attachment: AcroHealth_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: internal: Proposed language for credit rebalancing + holding mechanism (draft)

Team —

I've reviewed Acro's redline and sketched a compromise that protects revenue recognition and limits our exposure while meeting AcroHealth's forecasting needs. Attached is the small-playbook workbook (redwood_credit_playbook_draft.xlsx) with three options and suggested text edits. Summary: 

Option A (preferred): Tiered release + mutual true-up - Release schedule: 70% at contract Effective Date, 30% at the end of Quarter 2 post-Effective Date provided that cumulative documented usage >= 60% of committed Tier 1 volume; otherwise the remainder is released on a pro-rata basis within 45 days of reconciliation.
- True-up: Mutual true-up based on usage reports and our audit logs; both parties have 30 days to raise disputes; disputed amounts to be escrowed and resolved within 90 days.

Option B: Escrow holdback (compromise) - 10% of packaging credits placed into escrow holdback for 2 quarters; holdback released in two equal installments conditional on integration milestones and minimum monthly usage thresholds. This gives AcroHealth forecast smoothing and us a runway to validate integration.

Key legal edits (redline text suggestions):
- Replace unilateral clawback language in Section 4.3 with: "For disputed adjustments, the parties will perform a mutual reconciliation within 45 days following the end of the applicable calendar quarter. Any amounts that remain unresolved after 90 days will be retained in escrow pending final resolution."
- Add definition: "Packaging Credits" means one-time credits applied to the invoice schedule for SKU packaging and shall be recognized for revenue as set forth in Exhibit B.

Finance notes (Ben): I left a comment in the workbook about revenue recognition timing — moving to 70/30 shifts some revenue into later quarters; impact is manageable for this account but we should avoid open-ended escrow windows.

If you want to present Option A as the primary compromise with Option B as fallback, I can prepare a redlined Exhibit B and a short amendment memo to attach to the order form.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_credit_playbook_draft.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lewis <susan.lewis@acrohealth.com>, AcroHealth Procurement <procurement@acrohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T16:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging credit rebalancing — playbook errata (proposed compromise)

Susan —

Thanks again for the quick turnaround. Based on Marissa and Ben's input, here's a concise proposal that we believe meets your forecasting needs while keeping the order form executable on our end. If this looks good, we'll issue a short amendment and attach the redline for signature.

Proposal (summary):
- Release schedule: 70% of packaging credits at Effective Date; 30% released at end of Q2 post-Effective Date conditional on cumulative documented usage >= 60% of committed Tier 1 volume. If threshold not met, remaining credits released on a pro-rata basis within 45 days after reconciliation.
- Mutual true-up: Parties perform reconciliation within 45 days of quarter end; parties have 30 days to raise disputes; unresolved amounts go to escrow and are resolved within 90 days.
- Escrow holdback: We will accept up to a 10% escrow holdback for the first 2 quarters for the initial integration; escrow to be released in two equal installments upon meeting predefined integration milestones (detailed in the amendment).

Next steps:
1) Marissa will produce a concise amendment and a redline of Exhibit B (2-3 paragraphs) reflecting the above.
2) Ben will confirm final P&L impact (Ben: can you confirm the revenue recognition note and whether we need CFO approval for the escrow?)
3) If AcroHealth agrees, we will send the DocuSign packet for signature (expected turn: 48 hours).

Susan, can you confirm by 2026-11-22 whether AcroHealth prefers Option A (70/30 + mutual true-up) or Option B (10% escrow + milestones)? Happy to hop on a 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
